pr_title: gh gist delete: prompt for gist id
pr_body:
Fixes #10073.

This changes `gh gist delete` to prompt the user to select a gist when no args are passed, instead of returning a message with usage info. And adds a confirm flag to prompt for confirmation. The code for prompting is already used by other commands (used `gh gist view` and `gh repo delete` for reference).
pr_comments: Planning to add a prompt to confirm deletion as requested in #10073.

issue_context.title: `gh gist delete` does not prompt for a gist to delete or prompt for confirmation before deletion
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

- `gh gist delete` doesn't prompt for a gist to delete. This seems like it might be an oversight when compared to the behavior of other `gh gist` and `gh <some-command> delete` operations.
- `gh gist delete` should prompt for a gist to delete and confirm the selection to delete.
- `gh gist delete` also does not currently support `--yes` for non-interactive confirmation - perhaps it should? 

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

```
gh gist delete
```
### Expected vs actual behavior

**Expected**

```
❯ gh gist delete
? Select a gist to delete [Use arrows to move, type to filter]
> test.md test gist about 4 days ago
  draft.md  about 2 months ago
? Are you sure you want to delete gist test.md (Y/n)
```

**Actual**
```
gh gist delete
❯ gh gist delete
cannot delete: gist argument required

Usage:  gh gist delete {<id> | <url>} [flags]
```

### Notes

Discovered in #10042
comments: [Search across open source repos using `gh gist delete`...](https://github.com/search?q=%22gh+gist+delete%22&type=code)

> gh gist delete doesn't prompt for a gist to delete. This seems like it might be an oversight when compared to the behavior of other gh gist and gh <some-command> delete operations.

Might be an oversight. I'm not sure I'd consider it a bug. It seems like a pretty reasonable enhancement request though.

> gh gist delete should prompt for a gist to delete and confirm the selection to delete.

Do you think it's valuable to have a confirmation when the user just confirmed it via the selection itself?

> gh gist delete also does not currently support --yes for non-interactive confirmation - perhaps it should?

Do you think it's worth breaking non-interactive scripts by requiring this. I can see a good argument for it.

Thanks @williammartin ✨ 

> Might be an oversight. I'm not sure I'd consider it a bug. It seems like a pretty reasonable enhancement request though.

I think we're on the same page, but I've typically considered oversight = unintended behavior = bug. I don't care much about the labels though, either one makes sense to me 😁 

> Do you think it's valuable to have a confirmation when the user just confirmed it via the selection itself?

I was thinking of `repo delete` for this design consideration. We do have a second confirmation prompt for `repo delete`:

https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/253b08260025195c5f0b3987cdb6193ddbf5fa0e/pkg/cmd/repo/delete/delete.go#L105-L109

I'm not sure how valuable it is for a gist, though. The consideration being: I'm not aware of any (easy) way a gist deletion is reversed. A quick google [suggests a support ticket is required](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/27300913/is-it-possible-to-recover-a-deleted-gist-on-github).

For that reason, if I were choosing how to design this from the ground up, I would have added a confirmation same as repo delete.

> Do you think it's worth breaking non-interactive scripts by requiring this. I can see a good argument for it.

I'm on the fence but leaning towards being okay breaking non-interactive scripts because:

- It's an easy change to add `--yes`
- I'd like to think gists are not "business critical" in that disruptions to that flow are not critical
    - Even if that were the case, temporarily using an old release is within the options available to avoid affecting business. 
- The idea of having all our "delete" subcommands work similarly across the CLI is attractive

I see this issue report is no longer labeled as a bug but I came across the issue myself and it also seemed like a good first issue and I wanted to try to help out. I have a PR ready to add the selection prompt and confirm deletion. One thing I did differently, instead of the proposed deletion prompt `? Are you sure you want to delete gist test.md (Y/n)`, I use the pre-existing `ConfirmDeletion` prompt mentioned above from `repo delete`, and just gave it a `"delete"` string instead of the long `gistID`. So it looks like `? Type delete to confirm deletion:`. I think this is a good choice since gist file names are not unique. 

Please see proposed fix https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/10154

Thanks for the contribution, @danochoa. We're going to hammer out the final design of this then give your PR a review. I've already taken a look at it, and I doubt much will change, but keep your eye out for a follow up comment on this with the final design.

I'll add that generally we prefer folks work on issues labeled with `help-wanted`. Since this one is still labeled `needs-triage`, there's a chance that things will change from the initial issue post, and that could result in changes in your PR. We've had instances where the PR had to be thrown out completely and started anew. This can be a bad experience for contributors, and the `help-wanted` label helps us avoid that. Again, I doubt that's the case here, but just wanted to let you know for when you pick up your next issue 😉

@jtmcg Looking forward to seeing the final design and happy to make adjustments as needed. Thanks for taking a look.

I have seen the contributing page and will focus on `help-wanted` issues moving forward.
Removed `needs-user-input` - hoping to get more team feedback on AC for this 🙌
@williammartin bump - hoping to unblock this for @danochoa with your feedback on the A/C as FR please 🙏

## Acceptance Criteria

**When**: I run `gh gist delete --help`
**Then**: I see an informative help usage containing new `--yes` flag

```shell
Delete a gist

USAGE
  gh gist delete {<id> | <url>} [flags]

FLAGS
  --yes   confirm deletion without prompting

INHERITED FLAGS
  --help   Show help for command
```

---

**Given**: I have authenticated with `gist` scope
**And Given**: I have created a gist through GitHub UI or `gh gist create`
**When**: I run `gh gist delete <id>` interactively
**Then**: I see a prompt asking for confirmation of deleting gist including the gist description

```shell
? Delete <description> gist?
```

**When**: I confirm deletion of gist
**Then**: I see an informational message confirming the gist was deleted

```shell
✓ Gist "<description>" deleted
```

**When**: I cancel deletion of gist
**Then**: I see no message but receive exit code of `2` signaling the cancellation

> [!NOTE]
> For example, see [`gh release delete` behavior](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/40984d1eb6a3fb75df22da8eb5a5414c40c6d245/pkg/cmd/release/delete/delete.go#L83-L93)

---

**When**: I run `gh gist delete` non-interactively
**Then**: I see an informational message stating `--yes` flag is required to delete gist non-interactively followed by the usage statement

```shell
--yes required when not running interactively

Usage: ...
```

> [!NOTE]
> For examples, see [`gh label delete` behavior](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/5402e207ee89f2f3dc52779c3edde632485074cd/pkg/cmd/label/delete.go#L44-L46)

@danochoa : You should be good to go with acceptance criteria in https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/10073#issuecomment-2576159376.  Also, I've assigned this issue to you, helping avoid others from spinning their wheels while you're working on it. 👍 

Thanks again for your time contributing to the GitHub CLI! ❤

@andyfeller Thanks for the AC and for assigning to me. I will get to work on the requested changes.

One thing I want to confirm: Are you sure you want to use the gist `<description>` in the confirmation prompt and informational message? I wasn't sure that was a good idea since gist descriptions are optional and default to an empty string. Maybe I missed something but `gh release delete <tag>` relies on a required tag for the prompts and I haven't found a gh command that uses an optional field in the prompt.
I went ahead and completed the changes to meet the acceptance criteria. Please review when you get a chance. Thanks!

Btw here's what the output looks like with a default/blank description:

```
➜  cli git:(gh-gist-delete-prompt) ✗ bin/gh gist delete
? Select a gist gistfile0.txt  about 7 hours ago
? Delete "" gist? Yes
✓ Gist "" deleted
➜  cli git:(gh-gist-delete-prompt) ✗
```

I think the gist id or filename might be a better choice. Let me know if I should make that quick change. Thanks.

@danochoa, good callout on the UX. Given that the gist listing UX is currently designed to output `filename description`, I think mirroring the filename in the confirmation and success info is probably the right choice. I'd modify @andyfeller's AC to:

> **Given**: I have authenticated with gist scope
> **And Given**: I have created a gist through GitHub UI or gh gist create
> **When**: I run gh gist delete <id> interactively
> **Then**: I see a prompt asking for confirmation of deleting gist including the gist description
> 
> ```sh
> ? Delete <filename> gist?
> ```
> 
> **When**: I confirm deletion of gist
> **Then**: I see an informational message confirming the gist was deleted
> 
> ```sh
> ✓ Gist "<filename>" deleted
> ```

So the final UX is

```sh
$ gh gist delete
? Select a gist gistfile0.txt  about 7 hours ago
? Delete "gistfile0.txt" gist? Yes
✓ Gist "gistfile0.txt" deleted
```

@jtmcg Keeping the UX consistent with the listing output of `filename description` sounds good and mirroring the full filename and description in the gist delete confirmation info is probably not a bad idea, if there's no strong reason to drop the description. With `gistfile0.txt` as the default filename when creating gists, the description (if available) helps to identify a gist and provide a more useful prompt. There's also the case of gists with multiple files, referring to them as simply the first filename and description (as [here](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/4c8d124d370f9f58d9a8d8d5a5b590f409542bbe/pkg/cmd/gist/shared/shared.go#L232)) seems ok, otherwise may be improved by including a list of filenames, since a single filename may be misleading. I'll go ahead and make the changes to keep consistent with the full `filename description` in the confirmation and success info. Open to suggestions for improvement.

> [@jtmcg](https://github.com/jtmcg) Keeping the UX consistent with the listing output of `filename description` sounds good and mirroring the full filename and description in the gist delete confirmation info is probably not a bad idea, if there's no strong reason to drop the description.

I'm not sure we need both the filename and the description in the confirmation prompt. The selector visually distinguishes the filename from the description but the confirmation prompt does not (see screenshot). I think dropping the description in the confirmation prompt is better, because it is both shorter and the filename/description are preserved from the selection step above.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1ad124f2-cf31-4c38-a881-ae285b81b509)

> There's also the case of gists with multiple files, referring to them as simply the first filename and description (as [here](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/4c8d124d370f9f58d9a8d8d5a5b590f409542bbe/pkg/cmd/gist/shared/shared.go#L232)) seems ok, otherwise may be improved by including a list of filenames, since a single filename may be misleading.

Yeah, I agree, but since this is a current limitation of the existing `PromptGists` prompt I'm not keen on solving the multiple file problem in this issue 😅 Totally comfortable with filename + description here in the selector 👍 

Besides the one change to the confirmation prompt, this is super close 🙌 I'm reviewing your PR for other things besides this small UX change as well. Thanks for the patience and back and forth - you've been great to work with 🙂

Sounds good to me. I've removed the description from the prompts in 5de282c9702ca98bac0e4282bdb3ca6b12b40e71. Just need clarification on how to proceed re: [removing the prompter](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/10154#discussion_r1911069290) in the tests. It's been great working with you as well. Thanks.
